budget.rationale: The eight categories reconcile exactly to $11,650–$16,000. The low case slips just under the $12k target, but the credible high case reaches ~$16,000 — above the $15k strongly preferred maximum — driven by the transatlantic PIT–Athens airfare and peak-season island lodging. By the budget rubric, a high case above the preferred maximum scores 1. Cost never hides the trip, but it is the honest reason it is not ranked higher, and it is consistent with the other expensive-air island plans (e.g. greece-via-lisbon at $16,900).

weather.rationale: June in the Cyclades is hot, dry, and reliably sunny with a warming ~72°F sea, and it sits in the calm shoulder before the July–August meltemi peak. The score is held to 3 because the north/west coasts (Naxos beaches, Sarakiniko, Kleftiko) are exposed to an afternoon meltemi that requires managing — swim early, keep sheltered picks ready — rather than a clean 4.

swim.rationale: This is the strongest family swimming on the board short of the tropics: Naxos's Agios Prokopios and Plaka are long, shallow, sandy Blue-Flag beaches, Paros's Kolymbithres offers sheltered turquoise coves, and Milos adds boat-day and moonscape swims. The water is honestly ~22°C / 72°F in June — comfortable and warming, warm-ish rather than bathwater, and breezier than the Ionian — so it earns a 4 on beach quality, variety, and access rather than a 5 on temperature.

variety.rationale: Athens antiquity, Naxos's sandy beaches and green mountain villages, Paros's fishing harbor and granite coves, and Milos's volcanic moonscape and sea caves are four genuinely distinct experiences — culture, family beaches, a pretty harbor, and a wild volcanic finale — with no island repeating another.

ease.rationale: Naxos as a four-night anchor and a clean southwest arc keep it manageable, but this is honestly a mid-load plan: four bases, three inter-island ferries, a domestic flight, and a separate rental car on each island is more logistics than a single-island or one-car trip. It scores 3, not lower, because the sequence backtracks little and the Athens buffer night absorbs the fragile final connection.

food.rationale: Every base (Athens, Naxos, Paros, Milos) has supermarkets plus tavernas that reliably serve gyros, pizza, pasta, grilled meat, and fries — named venues (Pita Frank, Cuore Rosso, Caya, Egoist) confirm plain-food fallbacks throughout — strong picky-eater coverage that falls short of a 5 only on the remoteness of some island dinners.

risk.rationale: The defining risk is the meltemi: three inter-island ferries plus the Kleftiko boat can be disrupted by a strong north wind, and Milos's coves are exposed. It scores 3 rather than lower because June is the calm shoulder (the meltemi peaks in July–August, cancellations are uncommon), high-speed ferries usually run, and the plan builds in mitigations — a flex day, three Milos nights so the Kleftiko cruise can slide, and an Athens buffer night before the Atlantic flight.

nights.rationale: Twelve hotel nights (Athens 2 + Naxos 4 + Paros 2 + Milos 3 + Athens 1 buffer), which scores 5 on the 12+ rubric.

novelty.rationale: Greece is already represented on the board via the Crete-focused greece-via-lisbon plan, so this is not a wholly new country. But the Cyclades — Athens, Naxos, Paros, Milos — are an entirely distinct region and island set from Crete, with no overlap against the documented visited-place list, so it scores 4 (mostly new, one visited destination type/country) rather than 5.

pto.rationale: About 8 PTO days (Jun 9, 10, 11, 14, 15, 16, 17, 21), with weekends Jun 12–13 and 19–20 free and the Kleftiko boat day landing on Juneteenth-observed Friday Jun 18 at no PTO cost. Middle-of-the-pack PTO efficiency; displayed but zero-weighted in the total.
